subject: Hospitality
title: Personalization vs. Privacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Personalization vs. Privacy.

hook.text: Hotels know your pillow preference, your minibar choices, and when you wake up. Helpful or creepy? It depends on how they use it.

buildup.text: Personalization vs. Privacy sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: When personalization feels natural—'We remember you prefer extra pillows'—guests love it. It signals care and attention.

twist.text: When personalization feels invasive—'We noticed you searched for flights to Paris'—guests feel surveilled. The line is thin.

climax.text: The rule: use data to enhance, not exhibit. Guests should feel known, not watched. Show the benefit, hide the database.

punchline.text: Remember their pillows, forget the database. Personalization should feel like magic.

quiz.question: What is the key rule for hotel personalization?
options: Show guests all the data you have
Use data to enhance experience invisibly—guests should feel known, not watched
